title: Bellarmino: feast-honor terminates also on the Saints secondarily—dulia under ‘religion’ in the general sense
source_text: XXVII. Sed pertendunt alii, ac praecipue Bellarminus, honorem dierum festorum immediate & terminative pertinere etiam ad Sanctos, quanquam ad Deum primario, ad Sanctos tantum secundario spectet. Cujusmodi cultum dicunt esse duliae, non Latriae, & proinde religionis quidem cultum; sed religionis, non ut est nomen specialis virtutis, quae hominem erga Dei cultum bene disponit, sed ut est nomen generale. Sicut videre est apud Bellarminum de cultu Sanctorum lib. 3. cap. 16.
pass_a_gloss: But others contend, and especially Bellarmine, that the honor of feast days pertains immediately and terminatively also to the Saints, although it looks primarily to God, to the Saints only secondarily. Which kind of cult they say is of dulia, not of Latria, and therefore indeed a cult of religion; but of religion, not as it is the name of a special virtue which well disposes a man toward the cult of God, but as it is a general name. As is to be seen in Bellarmine On the Cult of the Saints, book 3, chapter 16.
pass_b_english: Bellarmino lets feast-honor terminate on Saints too—primarily God, secondarily Saints.
He calls that dulia, and ‘religion’ only in the broad genus, not the special Godward virtue.

choices.why: Saints as secondary terminus of feast-honor.
